audit_findings.title: Post-close Autronica financing and cash use are absent from the valued claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $555 million purchase price, equal to 15.9% of the $3.492 billion base equity value; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds pre-close cash, while owner earnings omit incremental borrowing costs and Autronica earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: A significant portion of our debt bears interest at variable rates that may increase in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch: Autronica had closed before the valuation date, but the valuation combines pre-close operating earnings and balance-sheet amounts. Cash consumption and interest expense would reduce value, while acquired earnings would increase it. A transaction equal to 15.9% of base equity value is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-close sources and uses, cash, debt, borrowing rates, purchase accounting and Autronica operating results; rerun a consistent post-close combined-equity valuation.

audit_findings.title: Large retained PFAS litigation exposure is not quantified in owner earnings or the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued settlements, judgments, uninsured defense costs or indemnity shortfalls would reduce future owner earnings or require a liability deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 4, 2026, Globe was named as a defendant in approximately 1,288 lawsuits comprised of about 22,090 claims based on a largely common set of assertions, predominantly styled as individual personal injury claims and including several putative class actions.
audit_findings.explanation: The retained exposure is demonstrated, with 1,222 lawsuits comprising 21,372 claims reported as of July 27, 2026, but the filing supplies no accrued loss or reasonably possible loss range. Defense costs incurred to date are already reflected in earnings; additional economic loss remains an unresolved possibility whose materiality cannot be established from claim counts alone.
audit_findings.action: Obtain accruals, reasonably possible loss ranges, defense-cost history, insurance limits and exclusions, supplier indemnities, and settlement or bellwether-case developments; rerun OE and the bridge if a supportable expected loss emerges.

audit_findings.title: Non-service pension income may be capitalized while required cash funding is omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 non-service benefit income of $20.339 million versus $7.028 million of pension contributions, a $13.311 million difference equal to 5.7% of the $234.3 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Accounting pension income can raise the OE numerator, while actual or sustainable pension funding should reduce cash available to owners.
audit_findings.evidence: Components of net periodic benefit (income) cost other than service cost are included in the line item Other income, net, and service costs are included in the line items Cost of products sold and Selling, general and administrative in the Consolidated Statements of Income.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the supplied OE calculation retained the accounting credit is unresolved because no pension reconciliation was provided. The filed amounts nevertheless establish a potentially material scale: the 2025 difference is 5.7% of anchor OE, and capitalizing it would affect both forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to pension service cost, non-service income, contributions and funded status; replace any included accounting pension income with a sustainable cash-funding requirement and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Legacy-liability indemnities retain counterparty and enforcement tail risk
audit_findings.mechanism: Counterparty failure, disputed indemnity coverage or enforcement costs could reduce OE or create a claim requiring deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The ability of MSA LLC and the Purchaser to honor their indemnity obligations is subject to commercial risk and, in addition, in the event of a dispute, the transaction, negotiated indemnities, and the extent of other legally available protections may be subject to future judicial interpretation.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual indemnities and their commercial and interpretation risks are demonstrated, but the record identifies no current default, retained loss, asserted indemnity dispute or measurable deterioration. This is an existing contingent risk rather than a demonstrated valuation error, and the record cannot establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Review current purchaser and MSA LLC solvency, capitalization, insurance assets, claim funding, indemnity payments, disputes and claims asserted against retained MSA entities; quantify and rerun if evidence of expected retained loss appears.

audit_findings.title: Outstanding cumulative preferred stock is missing from the common-equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: 18,342 net preferred shares at the $52.50 call price equal $962,955, or about $0.025 per diluted common share and 0.028% of the $3.492 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The preferred liquidation or call claim belongs ahead of common equity; recurring preferred dividends affect OE if not already deducted.
audit_findings.evidence: There were 71,340 shares issued and 52,998 shares held in treasury at both December 31, 2025 and 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is a demonstrated claim mismatch, although the filed $41,000 annual preferred dividend is already deducted in reported income available to common shareholders. Even deducting the full callable value would reduce base value by only about $0.025 per share, which is immaterial relative to the $89.31 base value per share and $188.69 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the OE series deducts preferred dividends and subtract $962,955 from the common-equity bridge if the preferred claim is not otherwise captured.
